summary: Runner label index corruption causing CI job misrouting and manual requeueing
description:
Issue summary:
During the 2026-03-10 release window we observed an increase in CI job failures that traced to incorrect routing of jobs to unavailable or wrong runners. The root cause appears to be corruption/staleness in the runner label index (the in-memory index used by the CI router to match job labels to runner capabilities).

Impact:
- ~12% of release pipeline jobs in us-east are routed to mismatched runners and fail pre-start health checks, resulting in manual requeues and delayed rollouts.
- Affected pipelines include multiple release branches and a few critical canary flows.

Environment:
- prod (us-east) CI cluster (k8s) running runner-service v3.7.1, ci-router v1.4.0, kvstore (etcd) v3.5

Observed behavior:
- Router returns a candidate runner list that lacks runners with the required label (e.g., "gpu:rtx-a100") or includes runners that have been decommissioned.
- Jobs enter "Pending" state, then fail with "RunnerCapabilityMismatch" or time out waiting for pod binding.
- Manual requeue usually schedules correctly after a short interval (30-90s).

Expected behavior:
- Router should consult fresh index and use up-to-date runner capabilities; decommissioned runners should never be selected.

Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Deploy a synthetic job with label set that matches a small subset of runners (e.g., "pool:release-canary, gpu:rtx-a100").
2) Simultaneously simulate a runner heartbeat gap by temporarily blocking runner-service-to-kvstore writes for ~45s.
3) Observe router candidate selection via debug endpoint (/debug/route) and compare to kvstore state.

Investigation notes:
- Heap snapshots and trace logs show duplicate keys and out-of-order index entries in the in-memory label index within runner-service. Suspect a race during incremental index rebuild when rapid runner heartbeat churn occurs.
- kvstore (etcd) data is correct; corruption is limited to the runner-service process memory index.
- A recent change in ci-router v1.4.0 introduced a quick-sync path that can trigger concurrent label-index merges; timeline aligns with when errors first appeared.
- No signs of disk corruption or network packet loss between services.

Logs and links:
- Grafana dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ci/router-health?orgId=1&var-region=us-east
- Trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/7f3a9c0b
- Slack thread: #internal-ci (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0CI12345/p1615567800000)
- Related PR currently under review: github.com/redwood-inference/ci-router/pull/1427

Workaround:
- Restarting runner-service pods in a rolling fashion forces a full index rebuild from kvstore and restores correct routing (temporary).
- Applying a short cooldown on heartbeat fast-syncs reduces incidence but does not fix the underlying race.

Immediate mitigation applied (2026-03-11):
- Scoped rollout: temporarily pinned ci-router to v1.3.9 for prod us-east.
- Added a conservative backoff on heartbeat-triggered index merges in runner-service config to reduce simultaneous merges.

Next steps / remediation plan:
- Engineering to reproduce in staging with a high-churn runner simulator to exercise the merge path. (Owner: Miguel Ortega)
- Add a unit/integration test that simulates concurrent merge operations and ensures index invariants. (Owner: Backend QA)
- Implement an atomic swap update for the in-memory index instead of in-place merges to eliminate the race. Target PR by 2026-03-18.
- Postfix: monitor for recurrence for 72 hours after code rollout; keep the temporary pinned ci-router version until fix validated.

Resolution: (pending)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a synthetic CI job with a narrow runner label set.
2) Induce runner heartbeat flare by restarting half of the runner pods quickly.
3) Observe routing differences between /debug/route and kvstore entries.
investigation_notes: Heap dumps show index entries with duplicate runner IDs under different label buckets. Concurrency window observed at index merge routine path mergeLabels(). Adding mutex reduced occurrence in local repro. Running more exhaustive fuzz tests in staging. Reference trace IDs included in logs_and_links.
